editorial_contributions.text: Summary: A dominating set \(D\) of a graph \(G=(V,E)\) is a split dominating set if the induced subgraph \(\langle V-D\rangle\) is disconnected. The split domination number \(\gamma_s(G)\) is the minimum cardinality of a split dominating set of \(G\). The set of vertices is a \(\gamma_s\)-set if it is split dominating set with \(\gamma_s(G)\). In this paper, we obtain the total number of \(\gamma_s\)-sets, the partially balanced incomplete block (PBIB)-designs on \(\gamma_s\)-sets of certain jump sizes of circulant graphs with \(m\)-association schemes for \(1\le m\le\lfloor\frac{p}{2}\rfloor\).

editorial_contributions.text:
For positive integers p and q, the Ramsey number r(p,q) is the least positive integer n such that any simple graph G of order n, either G contains a complete subgraph \(K_ p\) or a null (induced) subgraph \(N_ q.\) 


The known Ramsey numbers for p,q\(\geq 3\) are \(r(3,3)=6\), \(r(3,4)=9\), \(r(3,5)=14\), \(r(3,6)=18\), \(r(3,7)=23\), \(r(3,9)=36\) and \(r(4,4)=18\). Some lower bounds for certain Ramsey numbers are also known. 


The usual method used to find a lower bound for a Ramsey number is to construct a circulant graph \(G=G(Z_ n,S)\) where the vertex set V(G) of G is \(Z_ n=\{0,1,2,...,n-1\}\) which forms a group under addition modulo n, \(S\subseteq Z_ n\) is such that if \(s\in S\), then -s\(\in S\), and two vertices x and y of G are adjacent if and only if x-y\(\in S\). It is well known that circulant graphs are vertex-transitive and thus it is easier to show that the maximum size of an independent set of vertices in G cannot exceed a certain number. Also, G is triangle-free if S is sum- free, i.e. \(s+s'\not\in S\) for any \(s,s'\in S.\) 


The authors, with the help of computers, have constructed some circulant graphs \(G(Z_ n,S)\) where S is sum-free in \({\mathbb{Z}}_ n\), to determine the following new lower bounds for some Ramsey numbers: r(3,14)\(\geq 64\), r(3,15)\(\geq 73\), r(3,16)\(\geq 79\) and r(3,17)\(\geq 88\).

editorial_contributions.text: Summary: Two square \(0,1\)-matrices \(A\), \(B\) are a pair of Lehman matrices if \(AB^T= J+dI\), where \(J\) is the matrix of all 1s and \(d\) is a positive integer. It is known that there are infinitely many such matrices when \(d=1\), and these matrices are called thin Lehman matrices. An induced subgraph of the Johnson graph may be defined given any Lehman matrix, where the vertices of the graph correspond to rows of the matrix. These graphs are used to study thin Lehman matrices. We show that any connected component of such a graph determines the corresponding rows of the matrix up to permutations of the columns. We also provide a sharp bound on the maximum clique size of such graphs and give a complete classification of Lehman matrices whose graphs have at most two connected components. Some constraints on when a circulant matrix can be Lehman are also provided. Many general classes of thin Lehman matrices are constructed in the paper.

editorial_contributions.text: Summary: If every induced subgraph \(H\) of a graph \(G\) contains a minimal dominating set that intersects every maximal cliques of \(H\), then \(G\) is SSP (super strongly perfect). This paper presents a cyclic structure of some circulant graphs and later investigates their SSP properties, while also giving attention to find the SSP parameters like colourability, cardinality of minimal dominating set and number of maximal cliques of circulant graphs.
